content.value_statement: React and Next.js apps often lose speed through waterfalls, large bundles, and avoidable re-renders. This skill gives agents focused rules for reviewing and improving performance-sensitive code.
actual_capabilities: Identifies async waterfalls in React components, API routes, and Server Components.
Recommends direct imports, dynamic imports, and deferred third-party loading.
Explains caching choices with React.cache, LRU caches, SWR, and subscriptions.
Reviews re-render risks from state reads, effects, callbacks, and derived values.
Provides rendering and JavaScript micro-optimization rules with before-and-after examples.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not run benchmarks or profile applications.
Some recommendations depend on the project Next.js and React versions.
It does not replace security, accessibility, or product design review.
It may need adaptation for non-Vercel hosting or unusual build systems.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Find waterfalls, oversized imports, and re-render risks before a React or Next.js change ships.

use_cases.title: Refactor a Slow Page
use_cases.description: Apply Suspense, parallel fetching, caching, and bundle splitting to improve a slow user workflow.

use_cases.title: Plan Performance Work
use_cases.description: Turn broad performance goals into prioritized tasks across data fetching, bundles, rendering, and client state.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one React component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React component using the Vercel React best practices skill. List the highest impact performance issues first.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Next.js Route
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of data fetching and server work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Next.js route or Server Component for waterfalls, serialization size, caching, and non-blocking background work.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce Bundle Size
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these imports and client components for bundle size. Recommend direct imports, dynamic imports, and intent-based preloading where useful.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Refactor Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the React best practices rules to create a prioritized refactor plan. Include expected impact, affected files, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: A page fetches user data, configuration, and sidebar items one after another.
output: Start independent requests earlier so configuration and sidebar work do not wait on user data.
Move dependent work behind the exact value it needs instead of blocking the whole page.
Use a Suspense boundary when only one region needs slow data.

output_examples.input: A client component imports a heavy editor and several icons from package root entries.
output: Load the editor only when the user opens the editing workflow.
Use direct icon imports or package import optimization to reduce development and cold-start cost.
Preload the editor on hover or focus when the action is likely.

output_examples.input: A dashboard re-renders while the user resizes the browser and types into search.
output: Subscribe to a media query boolean instead of raw width values.
Use functional state updates for callbacks that depend on current state.
Narrow effect dependencies to primitive values used by the effect.

best_practices: Prioritize waterfall removal and bundle size before smaller JavaScript micro-optimizations.
Match each rule to the project runtime, framework version, and user-facing workflow.
Validate changes with profiling, build output, or focused regression tests after refactoring.
anti_patterns: Applying every rule mechanically without checking whether the code path is performance critical.
Adding memoization or caching without clear invalidation rules or measurable benefit.
Optimizing examples while ignoring accessibility, security, or correctness requirements.

faq.question: Does this skill change my code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides an agent that reviews or edits code in your environment.

faq.question: Is it only for Vercel deployments?
faq.answer: No. Most React and Next.js patterns apply broadly, but hosting details can change caching choices.

faq.question: Can it replace performance profiling?
faq.answer: No. It helps find likely issues, but profiling should confirm important changes.

faq.question: Does it cover React Server Components?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for server data fetching, serialization, Suspense, and caching.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: Only indirectly. Use a separate security review for data handling, scripts, and dependency risks.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
